title: The businessowners policy: Tony's Pizza's first year
summary: Replay Tony's Pizza's first year on a BOP: who can get one, the 80% rule, built-in Business Income, liability limits and Michigan's cancellation rule.
objectives: Recognize which businesses can and can't get a BOP
Apply the BOP's 80% replacement cost rule instead of coinsurance
Recall Business Income timing, liability aggregates and Michigan cancellation notice
Match Protective Safeguards, Utility Services and Hired and Non-Owned Auto to their jobs

scenes.title: Tony's Pizza gets a BOP
scenes.subtitle: 6% of your exam, about 9 items. Taught on the 2013 ISO form (BP 00 03 07 13); newer policies may differ

beats.text: What if Tony had started on a different policy? Rewind to opening week in Detroit: Dana sells Tony his insurance, and this year will test it.
beats.say: What if Tony had started on a different policy? Rewind to opening week in Detroit: Dana sells Tony his insurance, and this year will test it.

beats.text: Let's say his policy is on the 2013 ISO businessowners form. ISO's revised forms apply to Michigan policies written on or after July 1, 2025, so newer policies may differ. Businessowners questions are 6% of your exam, about 9 items.
beats.say: Let's say his policy is on the twenty thirteen I S O businessowners form. I S O's revised forms apply to Michigan policies written on or after July first, twenty twenty-five, so newer policies may differ. Businessowners questions are six percent of your exam, about nine items.

scenes.title: One policy, two big jobs
scenes.src: IRMI white paper 'Businessowners Policy Basics'; ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Secs. I-III; summary vs_commercial-05
scenes.plain: One policy that packages property and liability coverage for a small-to-medium business.
scenes.example: Tony's BOP covers his building, ovens and dough (property), and his liability if a customer slips and sues.
scenes.exam: Three sections: I Property, II Liability, III Common Policy Conditions.

beats.text: Dana's pick: a businessowners policy, or BOP. It packages property and liability for small-to-medium businesses.
beats.say: Dana's pick: a businessowners policy, or B O P. It packages property and liability for small-to-medium businesses.

beats.text: Tony's building, ovens and dough: the property side. A customer who slips and sues: the liability side.
beats.say: Tony's building, ovens and dough: the property side. A customer who slips and sues: the liability side.

beats.text: For the exam, know the BOP's three sections: Section I, Property; Section II, Liability; and Section III, Common Policy Conditions.
beats.say: For the exam, know the B O P's three sections: Section one, property; Section two, liability; and Section three, common policy conditions.

scenes.title: Who can get a BOP?
scenes.src: ISO BOP Program overview (Feb. 11, 2025), pp. 2-3; IRMI 'Businessowners Policy Basics'; question comm-051

cards.text: Tony's neighbor's tiny corner tavern. Six stools, spotless.
cards.why: An ordinary bar or tavern isn't an eligible BOP class at any size. Tiny doesn't help.

cards.text: A small apartment building in Lansing
cards.why: Apartments are an eligible BOP class.

cards.text: A small auto repair shop in Flint
cards.why: The 2025 program overview lists auto service risks as eligible. Older lists that exclude all auto repair are out of date.
Auto dealers remain ineligible, even though auto repair shops now qualify.

cards.text: A small light manufacturer in Holland
cards.why: The 2025 program overview lists light manufacturing as eligible. Older lists that exclude all manufacturers are out of date.

cards.text: A retail gift shop in Traverse City
cards.why: Retail stores are an eligible BOP class.

beats.text: I run the tiny tavern next door. Can I get one?
beats.say: I run the tiny tavern next door. Can I get one?

beats.text: Eligible classes include apartments, offices, retail stores and restaurants. But an ordinary bar or tavern isn't one, at any size, and neither is a car dealer.
beats.say: Eligible classes include apartments, offices, retail stores and restaurants. But an ordinary bar or tavern isn't one, at any size, and neither is a car dealer.

beats.text: ISO's 2025 overview lists auto repair and light manufacturing too. Your turn!
beats.say: I S O's twenty twenty-five overview lists auto repair and light manufacturing too. Your turn!

reveal.text: Tiny or not, taverns and car dealers can't. Old lists that ban all auto repair and manufacturers are out of date.
reveal.say: Tiny or not, taverns and car dealers can't. Old lists that ban all auto repair and manufacturers are out of date.

scenes.title: Section I: Tony's property
scenes.src: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.1, A.3, C.4-5; adapted from memory hook mn_comm-19

draw.text: BPP: +25% seasonal, if insured to 100% of average monthly values

beats.text: Section I covers Tony's building and business personal property, or BPP, like his register and stock. It's open perils: direct physical loss unless excluded or limited.
beats.say: Section one covers Tony's building and business personal property, or B P P, like his register and stock. It's open perils: direct physical loss unless excluded or limited.

beats.text: The building limit grows 8% a year, prorated, unless another percentage is shown.
beats.say: The building limit grows eight percent a year, prorated, unless another percentage is shown.

beats.text: Business personal property gets a 25% seasonal bump, if insured to 100% of average monthly values.
beats.say: Business personal property gets a twenty-five percent seasonal bump, if insured to one hundred percent of average monthly values.

scenes.title: Tony's fire alarm goes quiet
scenes.src: ISO IL 04 15 04 98, A.2, B.; BOP version BP 04 30 per FC&S (2020); question comm-056; card 31; memory hook mn_comm-20

draw.text: Tony's schedule: P-1 sprinklers, P-2 fire alarm. Others: P-3 security service, P-4 private fire department, and more
Fix it now, or after the rush?

beats.text: Dana adds Protective Safeguards: Tony must keep P-1, his sprinklers, and P-2, his fire alarm, working.
beats.say: Dana adds Protective Safeguards: Tony must keep P one, his sprinklers, and P two, his fire alarm, working.

beats.text: One Monday, the alarm stops reporting. What does Tony do?
beats.say: One Monday, the alarm stops reporting. What does Tony do?

options.label: Ignore it. Fire is covered anyway!
options.fail: Protective Safeguards excludes fire losses if you knew a listed safeguard was impaired and didn't tell the insurer, or didn't keep it working.

beats.text: Saturday, a grease fire! He knew the alarm was down and told no one: excluded.
beats.say: Saturday, a grease fire! He knew the alarm was down and told no one: excluded.

options.label: Tell the insurer, but skip the repair
options.fail: Two duties: report any impairment you know of, and keep listed safeguards you control in working order. Miss either one, and fire losses are excluded.

beats.text: Months later, a fire. Telling wasn't enough; he never fixed it: excluded.
beats.say: Months later, a fire. Telling wasn't enough; he never fixed it: excluded.

options.label: Fix it today, and tell the insurer
options.win: Keep listed safeguards you control in working order, and report any impairment you know of. Then the endorsement's fire exclusion doesn't apply.

beats.text: Fixed that afternoon, and the insurer knows.
beats.say: Fixed that afternoon, and the insurer knows.

beats.text: Both promises kept!
beats.say: Both promises kept!

reveal.text: Memory trick: P-1 pours water, P-2 phones it in, P-3 patrols, P-4 pays a private fire department. There are more symbols, too.
reveal.say: Memory trick: P one pours water, P two phones it in, P three patrols, P four pays a private fire department. There are more symbols, too.

scenes.title: The fire, and the generous cousin
scenes.src: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.5.c, A.6.a, A.6.e, C.2, D.3; ISO CP 00 10 10 12, A.4.c, A.5.a, A.5.c, C.; adapted from hook mn_comm-17

beats.text: Two months later: a Friday-night grease fire! The alarm calls it in.
beats.say: Two months later: a Friday-night grease fire! The alarm calls it in.

beats.text: The fire department service charge? The BOP pays up to $2,500; the 2012 commercial property form, $1,000.
beats.say: The fire department service charge? The B O P pays up to two thousand five hundred dollars; the twenty twelve commercial property form, one thousand dollars.

beats.text: The BOP is the generous cousin: valuable papers on premises get more, $10,000 versus $2,500. A newly acquired building gets the same in both: $250,000, for up to 30 days.
beats.say: The B O P is the generous cousin: valuable papers on premises get more, ten thousand dollars versus two thousand five hundred dollars. A newly acquired building gets the same in both: two hundred fifty thousand dollars, for up to thirty days.

beats.text: One stingy habit: a sign attached to the building gets $1,000, versus $2,500.
beats.say: One stingy habit: a sign attached to the building gets one thousand dollars, versus two thousand five hundred dollars.

scenes.title: Rebuilding the kitchen: the 80% rule
scenes.src: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I E.5.d(1); card 26; question comm-046; ACV: confusion pair cp_personal-05

draw.text: Walls: $60,000 to fix. ACV (worth after wear and tear): $40,000. Deductible ignored.

beats.text: The kitchen walls need $60,000 of repairs, done promptly. Their actual cash value, what they're worth after wear and tear, is $40,000. We'll ignore the deductible.
beats.say: The kitchen walls need sixty thousand dollars of repairs, done promptly. Their actual cash value, what they're worth after wear and tear, is forty thousand dollars. We'll ignore the deductible.

beats.text: The BOP has no coinsurance clause. Insure to at least 80% of replacement cost, and losses are paid at replacement cost.
beats.say: The B O P has no coinsurance clause. Insure to at least eighty percent of replacement cost, and losses are paid at replacement cost.

beats.text: Rebuilding the whole place costs $500,000, so Tony needs $400,000. His limit at the time of the fire is $300,000: 0.75 of what he needs.
beats.say: Rebuilding the whole place costs five hundred thousand dollars, so Tony needs four hundred thousand dollars. His limit at the time of the fire is three hundred thousand dollars: zero point seven five of what he needs.

beats.text: Fall short, and you get the bigger of actual cash value or a proportional share of the repair: here, $45,000. Your turn: slide Tony's limit down until actual cash value wins.
beats.say: Fall short, and you get the bigger of actual cash value or a proportional share of the repair: here, forty-five thousand dollars. Your turn: slide Tony's limit down until actual cash value wins.

reveal.text: Slide Tony's limit to $260,000: the proportional share is only $39,000, so actual cash value wins.
reveal.say: Slide Tony's limit to two hundred sixty thousand dollars: the proportional share is only thirty-nine thousand dollars, so actual cash value wins.

scenes.title: Closed for repairs, still getting paid
scenes.src: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.5.f-g, H.9; definitions: ISO CP 00 30 10 12, A.1-2; card 25; memory hook mn_comm-18
scenes.plain: Pays the income you lose while covered damage keeps your business closed.
scenes.example: Fire shuts Tony's kitchen for four months. After a 72-hour wait, Business Income pays the income he loses, within 12 months.
scenes.exam: 12 months; not subject to the Section I limits (no dollar limit). Business Income waits 72 hours; Extra Expense starts at once.

beats.text: The fire shuts Tony's own kitchen for four months. Business Income is built in: it pays the income he loses while covered damage keeps his business closed.
beats.say: The fire shuts Tony's own kitchen for four months. Business Income is built in: it pays the income he loses while covered damage keeps his business closed.

beats.text: Under the 2013 form: actual loss sustained, within 12 consecutive months, with no dollar limit.
beats.say: Under the twenty thirteen form: actual loss sustained, within twelve consecutive months, with no dollar limit.

beats.text: The catch: it starts 72 hours after the loss. Extra Expense, the extra cost to keep operating, starts immediately.
beats.say: The catch: it starts seventy-two hours after the loss. Extra Expense, the extra cost to keep operating, starts immediately.

beats.text: The exam's phrase for no dollar limit: not subject to the Section I limits.
beats.say: The exam's phrase for no dollar limit: not subject to the Section one limits.

scenes.title: Tony's call: wait, or keep cooking?
scenes.src: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.5.f-g, D.3, H.9; ISO CP 00 30 10 12, A.2; vs_commercial-05; hooks mn_comm-08, -18

beats.text: Day one: the church across the street offers to rent Tony its kitchen. What does he do?
beats.say: Day one: the church across the street offers to rent Tony its kitchen. What does he do?

options.label: Wait 72 hours. Nothing pays before that.
options.fail: The 72-hour wait applies to Business Income only. Extra Expense starts immediately, so it could have paid the rental from day one.

beats.text: Three days with a cold oven, and his regulars go elsewhere. Only Business Income waits 72 hours.
beats.say: Three days with a cold oven, and his regulars go elsewhere. Only Business Income waits seventy-two hours.

options.label: Call Dana to add business income first
options.fail: A BOP has Business Income and Extra Expense built in. In a commercial package policy, business income is a separate form you add.

beats.text: Tony calls Dana in a panic.
beats.say: Tony calls Dana in a panic.

beats.text: Tony, it's already built into your BOP!
beats.say: Tony, it's already built into your B O P!

draw.text: Built in: Business Income and Extra Expense

options.label: Rent the church kitchen today
options.win: Extra Expense starts immediately and pays the extra cost to keep operating. Business Income waits 72 hours.

beats.text: Pizzas roll out of the church kitchen. Extra Expense pays the rent, right away.
beats.say: Pizzas roll out of the church kitchen. Extra Expense pays the rent, right away.

reveal.text: Two sixties: ordinary payroll gets 60 days, and Extended Business Income up to 60 days after reopening, unless more are shown.
reveal.say: Two sixties: ordinary payroll gets sixty days, and Extended Business Income up to sixty days after reopening, unless more are shown.

reveal.text: Five skip the deductible: the fire department service charge, extinguisher recharge, Business Income, Extra Expense and Civil Authority.
reveal.say: Five skip the deductible: the fire department service charge, extinguisher recharge, Business Income, Extra Expense and Civil Authority.

scenes.title: Section II: a customer slips
scenes.src: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. II A.1-2, B.1.j, C., D.1-4; BP 04 04 per FC&S (2020); questions comm-052, comm-bop-12; card 33

draw.text: Who's an insured? Mirrors the CGL
Own car on the job: Hired and Non-Owned Auto

beats.text: Tony reopens, and a customer slips on the wet floor. Enter Section II: liability.
beats.say: Tony reopens, and a customer slips on the wet floor. Enter Section two: liability.

beats.text: Business Liability covers bodily injury, property damage, and personal and advertising injury. Medical Expenses pays accident bills within one year, regardless of fault. Who's an insured? It mirrors the CGL.
beats.say: Business Liability covers bodily injury, property damage, and personal and advertising injury. Medical Expenses pays accident bills within one year, regardless of fault. Who's an insured? It mirrors the C G L.

beats.text: There's one Liability and Medical Expenses limit, say $1,000,000. Both aggregates, general and products-completed operations, are twice that: $2,000,000 each.
beats.say: There's one Liability and Medical Expenses limit, say one million dollars. Both aggregates, general and products-completed operations, are twice that: two million dollars each.

beats.text: Professional services, like accounting, are excluded. And for drivers' own cars on the job, Tony adds Hired and Non-Owned Auto Liability.
beats.say: Professional services, like accounting, are excluded. And for drivers' own cars on the job, Tony adds Hired and Non-Owned Auto Liability.

scenes.title: Which coverage handles it?
scenes.src: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. II A.1-2, B.1.j; BP 04 04 per FC&S (2020); questions comm-053, comm-059, comm-bop-12; card 33

items.text: A customer slips on Tony's wet floor and sues him
items.why: A customer's bodily injury claim against Tony: Business Liability.

items.text: A diner trips at Tony's, no one at fault: her ER bill
items.why: Medical Expenses pays accident bills incurred and reported within one year, regardless of fault.

items.text: Tony's loose sign falls on a customer's car; she sues
items.why: Property damage to someone else's car: Business Liability.

items.text: An accounting firm's BOP: sued over a tax-return error
items.why: Professional services, like legal or accounting, are excluded. That needs professional liability coverage.

items.text: Tony's driver crashes her own car on a delivery; he's sued
items.why: Hired autos, and autos you don't own (like an employee's car) used in your business: Hired and Non-Owned Auto Liability.

beats.text: Your turn: which coverage handles each claim?
beats.say: Your turn: which coverage handles each claim?

reveal.text: Injuries and damage to others: Business Liability. Accident bills, regardless of fault: Medical Expenses.
reveal.say: Injuries and damage to others: Business Liability. Accident bills, regardless of fault: Medical Expenses.

scenes.title: One old substation, one big question
scenes.src: BP 04 56 and BP 04 57 per FC&S (2020); ISO BP 04 57 01 06; ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I B.1.e; cp_commercial-08; comm-057

beats.text: Dana spots a gap: the BOP excludes power failures that start off premises. Her fix, Utility Services, comes in two forms.
beats.say: Dana spots a gap: the B O P excludes power failures that start off premises. Her fix, Utility Services, comes in two forms.

beats.text: Direct Damage pays for property the outage damages. Time Element pays for lost time: income and extra expense.
beats.say: Direct Damage pays for property the outage damages. Time Element pays for lost time: income and extra expense.

beats.text: Say a fire at the old substation cuts Tony's power for a week. What pays his lost income?
beats.say: Say a fire at the old substation cuts Tony's power for a week. What pays his lost income?

options.label: Nothing extra: Business Income is built in
options.fail: The BOP excludes utility failures that start away from the premises. Lost income from one needs Utility Services, Time Element.

beats.text: Tony's goes dark. Built-in Business Income won't pay for an off-premises outage.
beats.say: Tony's goes dark. Built-in Business Income won't pay for an off-premises outage.

options.label: Utility Services, Direct Damage
options.fail: Direct Damage pays for damage to your covered property. Lost income and extra expense from the outage are Time Element.

beats.text: Dark again. Direct Damage pays for damaged property, not lost income.
beats.say: Dark again. Direct Damage pays for damaged property, not lost income.

options.label: Utility Services, Time Element
options.win: Time Element pays lost Business Income and Extra Expense when covered damage to scheduled off-premises utility property cuts your service.

beats.text: Power supply property is checked in his schedule, so Time Element covers his lost income.
beats.say: Power supply property is checked in his schedule, so Time Element covers his lost income.

reveal.text: Lost income: Time Element. And overhead transmission lines count only if scheduled.
reveal.say: Lost income: Time Element. And overhead transmission lines count only if scheduled.

scenes.title: Section III: how much warning?
scenes.src: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. III A.2; MCL 500.2833(1)(i); MCL 500.3020(1)(b); question comm-054; card 30
scenes.plain: The written warning an insurer must mail before it cancels your policy.
scenes.example: Dana's Bay City client has a building that's sat empty 70 days. The insurance company wants to cancel. How much warning does it owe?
scenes.exam: Form: 5 days for listed conditions, like 60 or more days vacant; 10 nonpayment; 30 other. Michigan: at least 10.

beats.text: Last, Section III: common policy conditions, like the rules for canceling. A cancellation notice is the written warning an insurer must mail before it cancels your policy.
beats.say: Last, Section three: common policy conditions, like the rules for canceling. A cancellation notice is the written warning an insurer must mail before it cancels your policy.

beats.text: Dana's Bay City client has a building that's sat empty 70 days. The insurance company wants to cancel. How much warning does it owe? The 2013 form allows 5 days' notice for certain building conditions, like 60 or more consecutive days vacant or unoccupied.
beats.say: Dana's Bay City client has a building that's sat empty seventy days. The insurance company wants to cancel. How much warning does it owe? The twenty thirteen form allows five days' notice for certain building conditions, like sixty or more consecutive days vacant or unoccupied.

beats.text: Otherwise, 10 days for nonpayment, 30 for other reasons. But in Michigan, the insurer must mail at least 10 days' notice, for fire or casualty insurance.
beats.say: Otherwise, ten days for nonpayment, thirty for other reasons. But in Michigan, the insurer must mail at least ten days' notice, for fire or casualty insurance.

scenes.q: The Bay City building, insured under the 2013 BOP form, has been vacant 70 consecutive days. In Michigan, the insurer must mail its cancellation notice at least how many days ahead?
scenes.why: Michigan law requires the insurer to mail cancellation notice at least 10 days before cancellation, for fire and casualty insurance. The form's 5 days isn't enough.

beats.text: Back to Bay City. Pick an answer.
beats.say: Back to Bay City. Pick an answer.

reveal.text: 10 days. In Michigan, state law overrides the form's 5 days.
reveal.say: Ten days. In Michigan, state law overrides the form's five days.

scenes.title: Key takeaways
items: Ordinary bar or tavern: no BOP at any size
No coinsurance clause: insure to 80% of replacement cost
Business Income: 12 months, no dollar limit, waits 72 hours
8, 25, times 2: building 8%, BPP 25%, aggregates twice the limit
Michigan: insurer cancellation needs at least 10 days' notice

beats.text: No BOP for an ordinary bar or tavern, at any size. No coinsurance clause: insure to 80% of replacement cost. Business Income: 12 months, no dollar limit, and it waits 72 hours.
beats.say: No B O P for an ordinary bar or tavern, at any size. No coinsurance clause: insure to eighty percent of replacement cost. Business Income: twelve months, no dollar limit, and it waits seventy-two hours.

beats.text: 8, 25, times 2: building 8%, BPP 25%, aggregates twice the limit. Michigan: insurer cancellation needs at least 10 days' notice.
beats.say: ... Eight... twenty-five... times two: building eight percent, B P P twenty-five percent, aggregates twice the limit. Michigan: insurer cancellation needs at least ten days' notice.

beats.text: Next year? I'm insuring to 80%.
beats.say: Next year? I'm insuring to eighty percent.
